about: Everything the one-line summary decides: which entries appear at all, when a list is too long to spell out, and how a positional is written. The collapse thresholds and the hidden-entry rules are the parts a real CLI exercises unevenly — mise has plenty of commands past the threshold and almost none sitting exactly on it.

vectors.doc: A default makes a positional optional, so it is square-bracketed however it was declared.
The ellipsis goes outside the brackets.
A positional that only takes what follows `--` shows the separator inside its brackets: one optional thing, not a literal `--` and then an optional word.
Three or more flags collapse to a placeholder rather than being spelled out.
The collapsed placeholder is angled when any of the flags it stands for is required.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--a"
flag "--b"
flag "--c <v>" required=#true

vectors.doc: Two is the limit, and at the limit the flags are still named.
Positionals collapse the same way, and the placeholder is always variadic.
Angled when any of the positionals it stands for is required.
A hidden flag is absent from the line, and does not count towards the collapse threshold either.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--a"
flag "--b"
flag "--secret" hide=#true

vectors.doc: A hidden required flag does not angle the placeholder for the visible ones: the line describes what a user is invited to type.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--a"
flag "--b"
flag "--c"
flag "--secret <v>" hide=#true required=#true

vectors.doc: A command with subcommands ends its line by saying so, whatever they are called.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
cmd "go" help="Go"
cmd "stop" help="Stop"

vectors.doc: The line is computed before hidden commands are filtered, so a command whose subcommands are all hidden still says `<SUBCOMMAND>` while listing none. Recorded because it looks like a bug and is the reference's behaviour, which mise reaches on `direnv` and `dotfiles`.
A subcommand's line names the whole path from the binary down, not the child's own name.
Flags come before positionals, each group collapsing on its own count.
